narrative_purpose: Break the intuition that one-way lungs belong only to flight: a bird, an alligator, and a monitor lizard carry the same functional airflow principle in very different bodies, making it plausible that the mechanism is ancient or repeatedly favoured rather than an aviation specialisation.
subject: Three living Earth vertebrates in matched side profile: a pigeon standing alert, an alligator resting low, and a monitor lizard walking; each has a restrained translucent thoracic window revealing the lungs, with a continuous ribbon of cool blue inhaled air entering, passing through the gas-exchange region in one direction, and leaving along a separate branch without reversing through the exchange tissue.
scene: A comparative respiratory-physiology plate against deep indigo, the three animals sharing one ground line but separated by dark breathing room.
camera: Clean lateral naturalist view at equal visual scale, with every thoracic window unobstructed.
light: Soft cool dorsal light on feathers, scales, and hide; the airflow ribbons and lung interiors glow faintly cyan from within; deep teal shadow elsewhere.
palette: Void indigo and ocean teal dominant, stone-grey animal surfaces, Pandora cyan airflow, scarce living green in the lung tissue.
style: Painterly comparative-anatomy naturalist plate, hand-painted, scientifically restrained and tactile.
detail_level: Crisp on the three lung windows and the continuous airflow paths; exterior anatomy stays observed but subordinate.
composition: Bird, alligator, and lizard arranged left to right with repeated thoracic windows at one visual height, making the shared flow pattern readable without labels.
consistency_notes: The blue airflow must form a continuous through-path across each gas-exchange region rather than a simple in-and-out tidal loop. Keep the animals recognisably pigeon, alligator, and monitor lizard.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no charts, no duplicated limbs, no fantasy reptiles, no photorealistic cutaway, no glossy 3D medical render, no cartoon or anime style
